sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Maxen, also called Macsen or Macsen Wledig, was a Welsh hero. He was a historical king and a Roman soldier from Spain. His Celtic origin is possible but unclear. Maxen moved to Britain around the year 383 and married a Celtic woman named Elen Lwddog. His legions proclaimed him emperor of Rome as Magnus Maximus. He led an assault on the continental Roman lands and finally on Rome itself. The usurping emperor drove Valentinian II from the city. Theodosius, the emperor of the eastern Roman territory, met Maxen in battle and defeated him. Maxen was put to death on July 28, 388. His widow Elen returned to Wales and became the ancestral mother of several dynasties. Maxen appears in Welsh literature in the visionary twelfth-century poem The Dream of Maxen.
objective: Document Maxen, the Welsh hero and emperor of the late Roman period.
